entries.title: Build Your Support Circle
entries.description: Move recovery out of isolation by making one intentional connection each day.
steps: List three safe people or resources.
Contact one person before a difficult moment.
End each day by noting where support helped.

entries.title: Bonus: Ten-Minute Pause
entries.description: Practice delaying urges long enough for choice to return.
steps: Set a ten-minute timer when an urge rises.
Breathe slowly and change your location.
Choose the next healthy action when the timer ends.

entries.title: Clear One Trigger
entries.description: Reduce one source of easy access to an old pattern and replace it with support.
steps: Identify one repeat trigger.
Remove or block its easiest access point.
Place a healthy alternative in the same path.

entries.title: Tell the Truth Gently
entries.description: Practice one honest recovery conversation without shame or exaggeration.
steps: Choose a trusted listener.
Name what happened and what you need.
Agree on one concrete follow-up.

entries.title: Morning Before Messages
entries.description: Give the first minutes of the day to grounding rather than urgency.
steps: Keep your phone out of reach overnight.
Read one recovery verse after waking.
Choose today’s support step before opening messages.

entries.title: Bonus: Craving Care Kit
entries.description: Prepare a small set of tools for high-pressure moments.
steps: Add water and a grounding reminder.
Save two support contacts.
Include one activity that changes your environment.

entries.title: Practice HALT Awareness
entries.description: Notice when hunger, anger, loneliness, or tiredness is increasing vulnerability.
steps: Check HALT at midday and evening.
Respond to the need before judging it.
Record which state most affects your choices.

entries.title: Replace, Don’t Just Remove
entries.description: Build a life-giving routine where an old habit used to live.
steps: Choose one high-risk time of day.
Plan a specific healthy replacement.
Repeat it at the same time for seven days.

entries.title: One Day of Clean Inputs
entries.description: Protect your attention from media or environments that intensify harmful urges.
steps: Identify triggering input.
Mute, unfollow, or avoid it for one day.
Fill the space with something peaceful and true.

entries.title: Bonus: Five Honest Minutes
entries.description: Use a short daily journal check-in to catch pressure before it grows.
steps: Name the strongest feeling.
Name the strongest urge.
Write the safest next action.

entries.title: Move Through the Urge
entries.description: Use gentle movement to lower stress and interrupt automatic behavior.
steps: Choose a safe ten-minute movement.
Begin when pressure rises, not after it peaks.
Notice how the urge changes before and after.

entries.title: Repair One Small Thing
entries.description: Strengthen recovery by taking one manageable step toward restored trust.
steps: Choose a repair that is safe and appropriate.
Own your part without demanding a response.
Let consistent action support your words.

entries.title: Protect Your Evening
entries.description: Create a calmer final hour that supports sleep and lowers late-day vulnerability.
steps: Set a stopping time for stimulating media.
Prepare tomorrow’s first healthy choice.
End with a brief prayer or breathing practice.

entries.title: Bonus: Gratitude Without Denial
entries.description: Notice what is good while remaining honest about what is hard.
steps: Name one difficult truth.
Name three sources of help or goodness.
Thank someone who supported your recovery.

entries.title: Ask Before the Crisis
entries.description: Reach for support while the pressure is still manageable.
steps: Rate pressure from one to ten each afternoon.
Contact support at five instead of waiting for nine.
Write down what made early help useful.

entries.title: Practice a Clean No
entries.description: Use a clear boundary to protect recovery without overexplaining.
steps: Identify one risky invitation or request.
Prepare a short respectful no.
Offer a safe alternative only if you want to.

entries.title: Serve Without Escaping
entries.description: Choose one act of service that connects you to purpose while honoring your limits.
steps: Choose a small useful act.
Keep the commitment realistic.
Reflect on the difference between service and avoidance.

entries.title: Bonus: Reset After a Slip
entries.description: Respond to a setback quickly with truth, support, and a renewed plan.
steps: Interrupt shame and tell the truth.
Contact support and reduce immediate risk.
Write one lesson and restart today.

entries.title: Celebrate Real Progress
entries.description: Recognize growth without waiting for perfection.
steps: List three changes you have practiced.
Thank someone who helped.
Choose the next milestone worth pursuing.

entries.title: Carry Hope Forward
entries.description: Build a simple plan for continuing recovery beyond this campaign.
steps: Keep the three tools that helped most.
Schedule your next support connection.
Write a promise to your future self.
